title: Relative ampleness is open on the base
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. If $x\in X$ and the restriction $\mathcal M|_{Y_x}$ to the fibre [def-pc-fibre-product] is ample in the absolute sense of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], then there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ in $X$ such that $f^{-1}(U)$ is quasi-compact and $\mathcal M|_{f^{-1}(U)}$ is ample on every inverse image of an affine open of $U$ (that is, it is relatively ample over $U$ in the stated sense).

proof.text: Choose an affine open neighbourhood $X^0$ of $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], the restriction $Y^0=f^{-1}(X^0)\to X^0$ is proper. Its fibre and restricted module at $x$ identify with the original ones by the fibre-product universal property. An open $U\subseteq X^0$ and its inverse images are also the corresponding opens in the original schemes, so it suffices to work over $X^0$. Rename the restricted data $f:Y\to X$ and $M$.

Apply [lem-trf-invertible-proper-noetherian-models] to the proper $f$, affine $X$, and invertible $M$. Obtain the small directed system with least element $0$, proper $f_i:Y_i\to X_i$, Noetherian stages, affine transitions and projections $a_i,b_i$, and invertible $M_0$ on $Y_0$. Put $M_i=q_{i0}^*M_0$; the cited statement gives $a_i^*M_i\cong M$ and $f_i a_i=b_i f$, as well as both limit cone properties.

proof.text: For the point $x$, Step 2 supplies every hypothesis of [lem-trf-model-fibre-ample-open], including the compatible line bundle and the Noetherian bases. The original hypothesis is precisely that $M|_{Y_x}$ is ample. Thus there are $i$ and an affine open neighbourhood $V_i$ of $x_i=b_i(x)$ with $M_i|_{f_i^{-1}(V_i)}$ ample in the absolute sense.

source.place: Tag 0D2S, lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood, proof: residue-field colimit, descent of fibre ampleness, and the Noetherian affine neighbourhood V_i.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-affine-square-ample-neighbourhood-transfer] to $a_i:Y\to Y_i$, $b_i:X\to X_i$, $f$, $f_i$, $M_i$, $M$, and $V_i$. Step 2 gives the affine horizontal maps, commuting equation and pullback isomorphism; Step 3 gives the ample restriction. It follows that $U=b_i^{-1}(V_i)$ is affine, $f^{-1}(U)$ is quasi-compact, and $M$ is ample on the inverse image of every affine open of $U$. Since $b_i(x)=x_i\in V_i$, $x\in U$. Together with Step 1 this proves the original statement.
